chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: Freelancing after Europe and joining Rose Murphy
summary: He hardly played with Parker and Gillespie beyond one record date; after 1948 he freelanced and worked about a year with pianist-singer Rose Murphy, including a trip to Australia.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now did you play with them much, other than in that jam situation and in that particular recording
Hardly at all. I was so busy with my own group or two and working, as I've said before, with Art Tatum, Slim Gaillard, a few others here and there, you know. Stayed fairly busy, you know.
Well, now, who did you work with when you came back from Europe? After 1948, after you returned from Europe, do you remember which bands you started working in then?
Well, I was here and there. I did a little stint with -- do you remember Rose Murphy?

She played piano and sang. I played with her for a little -- short while. They used to call her the Chi-Chi girl (Laughter.) -- where she used to sing her favorite number was 'I Can't Give You Anything But Love, Chi-Chi,' with a high voice? You may have heard. I played with her for, oh, about a year or so.
Yes, in the '50s. Yes, and we traveled quite a bit and a drummer or two joined us in our travels, you know. We played all over the country. In fact, we went as
Oh, you played in Australia, did you?
Do you remember about what year that was you went to Australia?
Now, that was around '59, I think.
